account:
Today has seemed mostly routine, though I still have a feeling that some town business may be passing me by. I have not found evidence of a secret gathering. At tea, my neighbour told me the baker described the bakery lanterns as welcoming lights, not lights for a special occasion; the neighbour knew of no planned gathering. The baker later reported steady business, thirty loaves sold by late afternoon, fresh bread still available, and no new riverside news. The baker offered to supply town-hall meetings. These statements do not establish any hidden purpose for the lanterns.

Freight has been advertising ferry crossings and deliveries from the ferry or east-landing warehouse, according to my neighbour. I heard some distant voices and shouting, including freight, but could not make out their words. I cannot infer what those conversations concerned. My neighbour also saw builder inspecting roads and the bridge, without personally seeing any hazards. I authorized only a visual bridge inspection, with two emeralds payable when the written report is delivered tomorrow at noon; no repairs or inn inspection were authorized. There was some uncertainty about an inn inspection, but I have no evidence that one was agreed.

Secretary has helped with appointments and records. I gave secretary one emerald for a writable book, and tonight secretary reported the office records and bridge authorization secured and the hall closed. Secretary reminded me of tomorrow's eight o'clock office appointment and ten o'clock mill grain inspection. I returned home for nineteen o'clock and tried to retire. Secretary has twice come to my door to check for final instructions, most recently saying my earlier reply was inaudible and promising to wait. My attempted instruction about leaving the builder's report at the office after lunch was not heard, so it is not an arrangement I can rely on. The repeated missed exchanges appear to be communication difficulties, not evidence of a scheme. I should answer secretary clearly, read my appointment book in the morning, and continue seeking firsthand news rather than treating my suspicions as facts.
